text:
NICE CG32 (2006; NICE surveillance in 2017 concluded no update was needed, and it remains current) covers oral nutrition support, enteral tube feeding and parenteral nutrition for malnourished or at-risk adults, including critically ill patients.

SCREENING: Screen all hospital inpatients on admission and repeat weekly; screen outpatients at first clinic appointment and care-home residents on admission and when there is concern. Consider nutrition support when a person is malnourished, defined as: BMI less than 18.5 kg/m2; unintentional weight loss greater than 10% within the last 3 to 6 months; or BMI less than 20 kg/m2 with unintentional weight loss greater than 5% within the last 3 to 6 months. Also consider it in people at risk: those who have eaten little or nothing for more than 5 days or are likely to do so, or who have poor absorptive capacity, high nutrient losses, or increased needs from catabolism.

CHOOSING THE ROUTE: Use oral, enteral or parenteral support alone or in combination, accounting for swallowing safety. Prefer enteral feeding when the gastrointestinal tract is functional and accessible; reserve parenteral nutrition for when enteral feeding is inadequate, unsafe or not tolerated.

REFEEDING SYNDROME PREVENTION: In people at high risk of refeeding problems, start feeding at a reduced rate and increase cautiously, with close electrolyte monitoring. Provide before and during the first 10 days of feeding: oral thiamin 200 to 300 mg daily; vitamin B co-strong 1 or 2 tablets 3 times a day (or full-dose daily intravenous vitamin B preparation if necessary); and a balanced multivitamin or trace-element supplement once daily. Give oral, enteral or intravenous potassium (likely requirement 2 to 4 mmol/kg/day), phosphate (likely requirement 0.3 to 0.6 mmol/kg/day) and magnesium (likely requirement 0.2 mmol/kg/day intravenous, 0.4 mmol/kg/day oral) unless pre-feeding plasma levels are high; correcting low pre-feeding levels beforehand is unnecessary.

MONITORING: Review indications, route, risks, benefits and goals at regular intervals, more often while unstable. Monitor nutritional, anthropometric, clinical and laboratory parameters per protocol — laboratory monitoring is especially relevant for parenteral nutrition and for metabolically unstable patients or those at risk of refeeding syndrome.
title: NICE CG32 — Nutrition support for adults: oral, enteral and parenteral nutrition
